title: Descent of a representable closed immersion along an auxiliary etale cover
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $E,B,Y$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], let $a:E\to B$ be representable, and let $b:B\to Y$ be any morphism. Let $(p_i:Y_i\to Y)_{i\in I}$ be a jointly surjective family [def-trf-algebraic-space-jointly-surjective-family] of representable etale maps from schemes. Put $B_i=B\times_YY_i$, $E_i=E\times_YY_i$, where $E\to Y$ is $b\circ a$, and let $a_i:E_i\to B_i$ be the base changes [def-pc-fibre-product]. Assume that, for every $i$ and every scheme $T_i\to B_i$, the represented scheme morphism $E_i\times_{B_i}T_i\to T_i$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then for every scheme $T\to B$ the represented scheme morphism $E\times_BT\to T$ is a closed immersion. Thus $a$ is a representable closed immersion; neither $E$ nor $B$ is required to be a scheme, and no finiteness condition on $I$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 03KD (lemma-descent-representable-transformations-property), closed-immersion specialization with cover pulled back from Y; scheme-test implementation uses descent.tex Tag 02L6 (lemma-descending-property-closed-immersion) and topologies.tex Tag 022C (lemma-zariski-etale-smooth-syntomic-fppf-fpqc).

proof.text: Fix a scheme $T$ and a map $t:T\to B$. Representability of $a$ gives a scheme $Z=E\times_BT$ and its projection $f:Z\to T$. Apply [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] to the cover $(Y_i\to Y)$ and the composite $b\circ t:T\to Y$. It gives schemes $U_i=T\times_YY_i$ and a jointly surjective etale family $q_i:U_i\to T$. Each $U_i$ has its canonical map $r_i:U_i\to B_i$, induced by $t$ and $U_i\to Y_i$.

source.place: Tag 041F (lemma-etale), part (3); scheme-test setup of spaces.tex Tag 03KD

proof.text: The universal properties of the fibre products identify $Z\times_TU_i$ with $E_i\times_{B_i}U_i$ over $U_i$. Explicitly, on any test scheme $V$ both sides consist of triples $(e,u,y_i)$ with $a(e)=t(u)$ and $b(t(u))=p_i(y_i)$; the two inverse maps retain these three entries. The projections to $U_i$ agree. The hypothesis applied to the scheme map $r_i:U_i\to B_i$ therefore says exactly that $f_i:Z\times_TU_i\to U_i$ is a closed immersion. Changing between these representing schemes does not change this property: a scheme isomorphism is a homeomorphism with isomorphisms on structure sheaves, so closed image and the defining surjections are preserved.

Regard $(q_i:U_i\to T)$ as a covering of the final object of the small etale site of $T$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. By [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-finer-than-etale], this same family is an fpqc covering of the scheme $T$. The statement applies to arbitrary covering families, so neither finiteness of $I$ nor quasi-compactness of the individual $q_i$ is required.

Apply [lem-pc-fpqc-descend-closed-immersion] to the scheme morphism $f:Z\to T$, its fpqc cover $(q_i)$, and the closed immersions $f_i$ proved above. It follows that $f$ is a closed immersion. Since $T\to B$ was arbitrary, every scheme test of $a$ is a closed immersion, which is the asserted representable closed-immersion property. If $I$ is empty, the pulled-back jointly surjective family forces $T$ to be empty; the same argument and the cited descent statement still apply.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q114-7df846237 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full: the item, and the statements of all 7 proof_deps and 5 stmt_deps. Sources read: Stacks spaces.tex 03KD (line 602) and descent.tex 02L6 (line 5968). The statement is unchanged from live and side-live, where the item is still unsplit with an empty proof. There are no new nodes and no repair note. Step 1: representability gives the scheme Z=E×_B T. The base-change and scheme clauses of lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers give schemes U_i=T×_Y Y_i that form a jointly surjective étale family. r_i=(t∘pr, pr) is well defined. Step 2 is elementary, and I verified the triple identification Z×_T U_i ≅ E_i×_{B_i} U_i on test schemes. The hypothesis is applied to the scheme map U_i→B_i, and a closed immersion stays one under composition with an isomorphism. Step 3: the q_i form an étale covering of T, and lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-finer-than-etale (arbitrary families) makes it an fpqc covering. Step 4: lem-pc-fpqc-descend-closed-immersion applies exactly, with no qc or finiteness hypothesis. Edge cases checked: empty I gives an empty T; the identity cover; B not a scheme; infinite I. There is no cycle among the 140 transitive dependencies. A duplicate search over about 58 nodes (representable, closed immersion, étale cover) found nothing that states this item. The tool_uses on lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-finer-than-etale and lem-pc-fpqc-descend-closed-immersion are accepted as generic tools.
